stage1_evidence_shown.label: BACKGROUND
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Avascular necrosis of bone (AVN) is a well known complication in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

stage1_evidence_shown.label: OBJECTIVE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To investigate the role of antiphospholipid antibody status (IgM and IgG anticardiolipin antibodies and lupus anticoagulant) with adjustment for corticosteroid use as risk factors for the development of AVN.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: METHODS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: A cohort of 265 patients receiving long term follow up in our SLE clinic from 1978 to 1998 was analysed. Patients with AVN complications were detected and then matched for age, sex, ethnicity, duration of disease, and organ disease with two other patients with SLE. A further 31 patients were chosen at random for the analysis.

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: Eleven patients had AVN, giving a point prevalence of 4%. There were no significant differences demonstrable in the presence of individual antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) or their combination between the group with AVN or the two control groups.
